bibliographic.title: The honeycomb and hyperhoneycomb polymorphs of IrI3

bibliographic.abstract: The synthesis of IrI3 at high pressure in its layered honeycomb polymorph is reported. Its crystal structure is refined by single crystal X-ray diffraction. Faults in the honeycomb layer stacking are observed by single crystal diffraction, synchrotron powder diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy. A previously unreported “hyperhoneycomb” polymorph of IrI3 (-IrI3), is also described - Its structure in space group F _ddd_ is determined by single crystal XRD. Both materials are highly-resistive diamagnetic semiconductors, consistent with a low spin _d_[6] configuration for Ir(III). The two- and three-dimensional Ir arrays in these polymorphs of IrI3 are analogous to those found in the _α-_ and _β-_ polymorphs of Li2IrO3, although the Ir electron configurations are different.

samples.sample_description: Monoclinic layered honeycomb structure IrI3 was obtained by quench cooling from 700 or 800 °C.
Orthorhombic IrI3 phase formed in high proportion by cooling at 50 °C/min from 800 °C, or either slowly cooling or quenching from 900 °C.

datasets.dataset_description: SCXRD data were collected on small crystals found in the polycrystalline products using graphite monochromated Mo Kα radiation.
Laboratory PXRD patterns were collected using Cu Kα radiation and used for Le Bail fitting of α-IrI3 and β-IrI3-dominated samples.
High-resolution synchrotron powder diffraction data for α-IrI3 were acquired at Beamline 11-BM at a wavelength of 0.4582 Å and showed asymmetric peak shapes characteristic of stacking faults.

TEM imaging, electron diffraction, and atomic-resolution high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy imaging were performed on thin α-IrI3 samples prepared by focused ion beam cutting.

Temperature-dependent Magnetization (M) data were collected under an applied field of 0.1 Tesla, and field-dependent magnetization of polycrystalline α-IrI3 powder was measured from -9 T to 9 T at two different temperatures.
Resistivity was measured on a dense polycrystalline piece of α-IrI3 and an as-made dense piece containing around 80% β-IrI3 over near-ambient temperature ranges.
Diffuse reflectance data were collected at ambient temperature on polycrystalline α- and β-IrI3-dominated samples and transferred to pseudo absorbance using Kubelka-Munk theory.
